name: Souvlaki
description: Small pieces of grilled meat, usually pork, on a skewer. Wrapped in pita with tomato, onion and tzatziki, it is Greece's favourite fast food.
how_to_eat: Eat the pita wrap by hand, or the skewers off the plate with chips.
how_to_order: Ask for 'souvlaki pita' at a souvlatzidiko (souvlaki shop).

name: Gyros
description: Meat (usually pork or chicken) cooked on a vertical rotisserie and shaved off in thin slices, served in pita with tomato, onion, chips and tzatziki. One of the most popular street foods in Greece.
how_to_eat: Eat wrapped in pita, by hand.
how_to_order: Order 'gyro pita' with 'pita me ola' for all the toppings.

name: Moussaka
description: Baked layers of aubergine (sometimes potato), spiced minced meat in tomato sauce and a thick béchamel topping. The Greek version was popularised in the 1920s by chef Nikolaos Tselementes.
how_to_order: Ask for 'moussaka' at tavernas, usually as a ready-cooked 'mageirefta' dish.

name: Pastitsio
description: Baked dish of tubular pasta, a spiced minced meat and tomato sauce, and a béchamel topping. A Sunday and taverna favourite throughout Greece.
how_to_order: Order by the portion at tavernas.

name: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
description: 'Village salad' of tomatoes, cucumber, onion, green pepper and olives topped with a slab of feta, dressed with olive oil and oregano. Served with almost every Greek meal.
how_to_eat: Mop up the oil and tomato juice with bread.
how_to_order: Ask for a 'horiatiki' at any taverna.

name: Tzatziki
description: Dip of strained yogurt, grated cucumber, garlic and olive oil. Served as a meze and as the sauce for souvlaki and gyros.
how_to_eat: Eat with bread or as a sauce on grilled meat.
how_to_order: Order as a meze at tavernas.

name: Lokma
description: Small deep-fried dough balls soaked in honey syrup and sprinkled with cinnamon and often chopped walnuts or sesame. A very old Greek sweet.
how_to_eat: Eat hot, straight from the fryer.
how_to_order: Buy a portion at a loukoumades shop.

name: Frappé
description: Foamy iced coffee made by shaking instant coffee with water and sugar, then adding ice and optionally milk. Invented in Thessaloniki in 1957, it became Greece's signature summer coffee.
how_to_eat: Sip slowly through a straw; Greeks make one last for hours.
how_to_order: Say how sweet: 'sketo' (no sugar), 'metrio' (medium) or 'glyko' (sweet), and 'me gala' for milk.

name: Savory_spinach_pie
description: Savoury pie of phyllo pastry filled with spinach, feta, onion, herbs and egg. Pies (pites) are a speciality of mainland Greece, especially Epirus.
how_to_eat: Eat warm or at room temperature, by the slice.
how_to_order: Buy a slice at a bakery (fournos) or order at tavernas.

name: Fasolada
description: Soup of white beans cooked with tomato, carrot, celery, onion and olive oil. Often called the national food of Greece, eaten especially during fasting periods.
how_to_eat: Eat with bread, olives and feta on the side.
how_to_order: Look for it as a daily dish in tavernas, especially in winter.

name: Gigantes Plaki
description: Large white 'giant' beans baked in a tomato sauce with onion, herbs and olive oil. A common meze and taverna dish.
how_to_order: Order as a meze or main at tavernas.

name: Stifado
description: Stew of beef or rabbit with lots of small whole onions, tomato, red wine and spices such as cinnamon and bay. A classic winter dish.
how_to_order: Ask for 'moschari stifado' (beef) or 'kouneli stifado' (rabbit).

name: Kleftiko
description: Lamb slow-cooked with garlic, lemon and herbs, traditionally sealed in a pit or wrapped in paper, until it falls off the bone. Named after the klephts, mountain rebels who hid their cooking.
how_to_order: Ask for 'arni kleftiko' at tavernas.

name: Galaktoboureko
description: Semolina custard baked between layers of buttered phyllo, then soaked in syrup. One of the most popular Greek syrup pastries.
how_to_order: Buy a piece at a zacharoplasteio (pastry shop).

name: Baklava of Ioannina
description: Layers of thin phyllo with chopped walnuts and almonds, baked with butter and soaked in syrup. Baklava is eaten across Greece; Ioannina in Epirus is especially known for its version.
how_to_order: Buy by the piece at pastry shops.

name: Diples
description: Thin sheets of egg dough folded and deep-fried into rolls or bows, then drizzled with honey and sprinkled with walnuts and cinnamon. Associated especially with the Peloponnese, and made for weddings and holidays.
how_to_order: Look for them in pastry shops in the Peloponnese.

name: Bougatsa
description: Phyllo pastry filled with semolina custard (or cheese or minced meat), served dusted with icing sugar and cinnamon. A breakfast institution in Thessaloniki.
how_to_eat: Eat warm for breakfast with coffee.
how_to_order: Order 'bougatsa me krema' (custard) at a bougatsa shop in Thessaloniki.

name: Koulouri Thessalonikis
description: Ring-shaped bread covered in sesame seeds, sold everywhere from street carts. The Thessaloniki version is a common quick breakfast.
how_to_eat: Eat on the go as breakfast.
how_to_order: Buy one from a street vendor or bakery.

name: Trigona Panoramatos
description: Triangular cones of crisp phyllo, soaked in syrup and filled with custard cream. They come from Panorama, a suburb of Thessaloniki.
how_to_order: Buy at pastry shops in Thessaloniki.

name: Soutzoukakia Smyrneika
description: Elongated meatballs spiced with cumin and garlic, cooked in tomato sauce. Brought by Greek refugees from Smyrna in the 1920s.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice or chips.
how_to_order: Order at tavernas and mageiria (cook-shops).

name: Tsipouro
description: Strong pomace brandy distilled from grape residue, plain or flavoured with anise. Its name has been EU-protected since 2006; it is made especially in Thessaly, Epirus and Macedonia.
how_to_eat: Drink in small glasses with a plate of meze; many add water or ice.
how_to_order: Order a 'karafaki' (small carafe) at a tsipouradiko, which brings free meze with each round.

name: Dakos
description: Barley rusk topped with grated tomato, crumbled mizithra or feta, olive oil, oregano and olives. A Cretan meze.
how_to_eat: Let the rusk soften in the tomato juice before eating.
how_to_order: Order as a meze at Cretan tavernas.

name: Kalitsounia
description: Small Cretan pies filled with soft cheese such as mizithra, sometimes with herbs, fried or baked. Made especially at Easter.
how_to_order: Buy at bakeries in Crete or order at tavernas.

name: Staka me Avga
description: Eggs fried in staka, a rich Cretan butter-fat made from the cream of sheep's or goat's milk. A traditional mountain dish.
how_to_eat: Scoop it up with bread.
how_to_order: Ask for 'staka me avga' at village tavernas.

name: Antikristo
description: Lamb or goat pieces skewered on long spits set around an open fire, cooked slowly with only salt. A traditional Cretan shepherds' method.
how_to_order: Order at Cretan tavernas, often in the mountain villages.

name: Sfakiani Pita
description: Thin pan-fried pie filled with mizithra cheese, served with honey drizzled on top. From the Sfakia region of Crete.
how_to_eat: Eat hot with honey.
how_to_order: Order at tavernas in Sfakia and around Chania.

name: Gamopilafo
description: 'Wedding pilaf': rice cooked in rich broth from boiled lamb, goat or rooster, finished with butter and lemon. Traditionally served at Cretan weddings.
how_to_order: Look for it at Cretan tavernas, especially in the mountain villages.

name: Tsikoudia (Raki)
description: Clear pomace brandy distilled from grape residue, without anise. Cretans call it raki and offer it as a sign of hospitality.
how_to_eat: Sip in small glasses, often offered free after a meal.
how_to_order: Ask for 'raki'; tavernas often bring it free with dessert.

name: Pastitsada
description: Rooster or beef braised in a spiced tomato sauce, served over thick pasta. A Corfiot dish showing Venetian influence.
how_to_order: Order at tavernas in Corfu.

name: Sofrito
description: Thin slices of veal cooked slowly in a white wine sauce with lots of garlic, vinegar and parsley. One of Corfu's best-known dishes.
how_to_eat: Eat with mashed potatoes or rice.
how_to_order: Order at Corfiot tavernas.

name: Bourdeto
description: Spicy fish stew, traditionally made with scorpionfish, cooked with lots of red pepper and onion. A Corfiot speciality.
how_to_order: Order at fish tavernas in Corfu.

name: Kumquat Liqueur
description: Sweet liqueur made from kumquats, which have been grown on Corfu since the British period. A signature souvenir of the island.
how_to_eat: Sip chilled after a meal.
how_to_order: Buy bottles in shops across Corfu.

name: Sykomaida
description: Dense cake of dried figs pressed with ouzo or grape must, pepper and spices, wrapped in fig leaves. A traditional Corfiot sweet.
how_to_eat: Eat in thin slices, e.g. with cheese or a drink.
how_to_order: Buy at Corfiot food shops.

name: Santorini Fava
description: Creamy purée of yellow split peas (Lathyrus) grown on Santorini, served with olive oil, raw onion and capers. 'Fava Santorinis' has EU Protected Designation of Origin status.
how_to_eat: Eat warm or at room temperature with bread.
how_to_order: Order as a meze at tavernas on Santorini.

name: Tomatokeftedes
description: Fritters of chopped Santorini cherry tomatoes, onion, mint and flour, fried in oil. A popular meze on Santorini.
how_to_order: Order as a meze at tavernas in the Cyclades.

name: Revithada
description: Chickpeas with onion and olive oil slow-baked overnight in a clay pot in a wood-fired oven. The traditional Sunday dish of Sifnos.
how_to_order: Look for it at tavernas on Sifnos, often on Sundays.

name: Melekouni
description: Bar of sesame seeds and almonds bound with honey, flavoured with orange and spices, traditionally given at weddings and baptisms. 'Melekouni' from Rhodes is an EU Protected Geographical Indication.
how_to_order: Buy wrapped bars in shops and bakeries on Rhodes.

name: Ouzo
description: Clear anise-flavoured spirit that turns milky white when mixed with water. Ouzo is an EU protected geographical indication for Greece and Cyprus; Plomari on Lesbos is its most famous production centre.
how_to_eat: Add water or ice and drink slowly with meze.
how_to_order: Order a small bottle ('karafaki') at an ouzeri, which serves meze with it.
